subject: SIG questionnaire + privacy/jurisdiction feasibility for MedSecure Health
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medsecure.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement <procurement@medsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:02:12 -0400
Subject: SIG request + HIPAA/BAA feasibility

Hi Neha —

Thanks for taking this on. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot ingesting clinical notes for a diagnostic assistant. Before we proceed we need a completed SIG questionnaire and a short feasibility confirmation on privacy/regulatory controls (GDPR/DPAs/SCCs and HIPAA/BAA). High-level asks:

- Can Redwood sign a BAA for processing PHI? If yes, are there deployment requirements (e.g., Dedicated or Private only)?
- For EU customers, how do you handle data transfers to US-hosted services — do you rely on SCCs, and are those SP-specific?
- Do you have SOC 2 Type II (or path to it) and can you share a report summary?

If you can send a completed SIG (we prefer the standard CAQ/SIG spreadsheet) and a draft DPA, that would be ideal. We may loop in our procurement and contracts teams.

Target timeline: we'd like the SIG answers and DPA in ~3–5 business days if possible.

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Lee
Director, Security & Compliance
MedSecure Health
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medsecure.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:15:40 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG request + HIPAA/BAA feasibility

Hi Sara —

Thanks — happy to coordinate. Short answers at a glance, more detail and a completed SIG attached (follow-up email):

- BAA: Redwood can support customers with PHI, but our standard approach is to provision a Dedicated or Private deployment for BAA-covered workloads (we do not recommend running PHI on the multi-tenant Hosted API for compliance reasons).
- EU transfers: we rely on SCCs for data transfers where customers instruct us to process EU personal data in US regions; we can provide SCCs text and execute via our DPA. For some customers we offer region-restricted processing (EU regions) to limit transfers.
- SOC 2: We maintain SOC 2 controls and have a Type II engagement; I will share a summary and the SOC 2 evidence items we can disclose.

A couple of clarifying questions to make the SIG precise:
1) Will MedSecure be sending raw PHI (identifiable clinical notes) or de-identified derivatives?
2) Which Redwood deployment are you planning to evaluate for the pilot (Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private)?
3) Any specific SIG control areas you want us to prioritize (encryption at rest, key management, audit logs, vendor management)?

I'll assemble the SIG responses and a DPA draft and get them over in the next 48–72 hours. If you prefer a quick call to walk through the technical controls, I'm available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 17:32:05 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG request + HIPAA/BAA feasibility (technical notes)

Neha / Kim — forwarding Sara's request with a few infra points for the SIG and DPA draft:

- For PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private; Dedicated gives us reserved GPU pools + isolated tenancy so data-in-transit and at-rest controls are straightforward. Private (VPC/on-prem) is available for customers requiring their own network controls.
- Key management: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private; Dedicated can use customer KMS via BYOK depending on contract.
- Auditability: per-route tracing + token-level logs are available; we'll need to document retention windows and access controls in the SIG.

Attaching a current network diagram that highlights cross-region routing and control-plane separation (network_diagram_v2.png).

If you want, I can draft the technical appendix for the DPA (data flow, subprocessor list, encryption coverage) — say the word and I'll prepare.

—Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medsecure.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement <procurement@medsecure.com>, Contracts <contracts@medsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 11:27:55 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG request + HIPAA/BAA feasibility

Thanks Neha — that helps. To answer your clarifying questions:
- We'll be sending raw clinical notes for the pilot (will involve identifiers).
- Pilot target: Dedicated if possible; if not, we may require Private depending on the DPA/BAA terms.
- Priority SIG areas: encryption at rest, key mgmt, access controls, audit logs, subprocessor list, incident response.

Please include the subprocessor list and any standard retention defaults you enforce. Also please send a draft DPA and indicate which clauses are negotiable (SCCs, data localization, breach notification timing). Procurement & Contracts are on copy — they'd like the SIG and DPA for their review.

Sara
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:45:12 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG request + HIPAA/BAA feasibility (legal touchpoints)

Neha / Marcus — quick legal checklist for the DPA/SIG:
- We'll mark BAA as available only for Dedicated/Private deployments and call out required technical controls (customer-managed keys or equivalent encryption assurance).
- SCCs: include standard EU SCCs text as an addendum and flag any subprocessor transfers to non-EU jurisdictions.
- Incident notification: recommend 72-hour SLA for notification to customer plus detailed follow-up timeline.

I can add redline comments to a DPA draft once you have v1.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medsecure.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Completed SIG + DPA draft for MedSecure pilot

Hi Sara / team —

Attached are: 1) redwood_SIG_answers.xlsx (completed SIG in standard spreadsheet format) and 2) redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (initial DPA including SCCs addendum). Highlights:

- BAA eligibility: Redwood will execute a BAA when the customer uses Dedicated or Private deployment. We call this out in section 3.2 of the DPA draft.
- SCCs & transfers: DPA includes SCCs addendum; for EU->US transfers we rely on SCCs unless the customer requires region-locked processing.
- SOC 2: I included a SOC 2 summary page in the DPA pack; full report can be shared under NDA.
- Key management: options documented (customer-managed KMS for Private; BYOK options for Dedicated where supported).
- Incident response: draft includes 72-hour initial notification and a 30-day remediation plan commitment for incidents impacting PHI.

Related links: I uploaded the working docs to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3example — please add comments on the SIG sheet where you'd like clarifications.

Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement/Contracts to review DPA & raise redlines (we can accept DocuSign or inline comments).
2) Technical call to review SIG answers and the technical appendix (Marcus and I can join) — I'm available Thu 24 Jul 10:00–12:00 ET or Fri 25 Jul 14:00–16:00 ET.

Thanks — attaching files as requested.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_SIG_answers.xlsx (sheet), redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf

Neha — thanks for the packet. A couple immediate asks from Contracts:

1) We need a SOC 2 Type II report (or a vendor-supplied summary plus auditor contact) to complete our risk review. Can Redwood share the report or an auditor attestation under NDA?
2) We want to review a BAA template. Does Redwood have standard BAA language we can review now?

Hi —

Thanks for the quick review. We can provide a SOC 2 Type II summary (attached: soc2-summary-2024.pdf) and can share the full report with your security team under NDA — please send the NDA contact or we can route through your secure upload.

We do have standard BAA language; I'll circulate a BAA template by end of day and flag the clauses that require Dedicated/Private deployment. For BYOK/KMS: Dedicated supports BYOK in most configurations; Private supports customer-managed KMS by default. There may be an incremental fee for managed BYOK in Dedicated depending on billing profile — Marcus and our sales team can confirm pricing.

I'll also schedule the technical review call — proposed Thu 24 Jul 10:00 ET was before Contracts' note, but Marcus and I can do Fri 25 Jul 14:00 ET if that works.

Neha

Redwood Inference
